title: Halloumi with tomato, carrot and chickpea salad

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is plain, whole food: fresh veg, tinned chickpeas, halloumi, olive oil, lemon, mint and ground cumin, with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Tesco sells every item at an everyday price, and a 250g block of halloumi is a normal weekly buy.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan, a grater and a bowl, and frying halloumi is well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: 500g tomatoes, three carrots, a tin of chickpeas, 250g halloumi and rocket make a sensible lunch for four, the dressing is in proportion, and 2 minutes a side colours the halloumi properly.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers wedging the tomatoes, grating three carrots, draining the chickpeas, zesting the lemon and slicing the halloumi, and 5 minutes matches the frying, so it suits a quick lunch.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and the steps add nothing that is not listed.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm tomato salad suits mid-June, and the 500g of tomato wedges make up the bulk of the dish even though halloumi leads the title.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Vegetables, chickpeas and halloumi make a filling, balanced lunch a family would happily eat again.
